title: Add optimization config version tables + migrations (immutable versions) and basic CRUD
author: Michael Nguyen
description: Context: As part of Safe apply + rollback for Optimize changes, we need immutable, versioned Optimization Config objects in the control plane. This PR adds the persistence layer (tables + migrations) and basic CRUD endpoints (internal for now) to create and retrieve versions. Scope: Hosted + Dedicated control plane. Private pinning/apply flows will come later. Summary of changes: 1) Database: Introduces `optimization_config_versions` as the immutable version record, and `optimization_config_active` as the per-scope pointer to the currently active version. Versions are append-only and cannot be mutated after creation; active pointer updates are transactional. 2) API (internal): Adds minimal CRUD routes to create a new version (POST), list versions (GET), and fetch a version by id/version number (GET). No diffing/semantic validation or rollout controller in this PR. 3) Service layer: Adds repository helpers with optimistic concurrency checks for pointer updates and a small amount of input validation (schema shape validation is deliberately shallow here; full semantic validators in ENG-4822). Data model details: - `optimization_config_versions`: (id UUID PK, config_key TEXT, version INT, scope JSONB, payload JSONB, payload_sha256 TEXT, created_by TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ, comment TEXT, source TEXT). Uniqueness constraint: (config_key, version). Secondary index: (config_key, created_at DESC). - `optimization_config_active`: (id UUID PK, config_key TEXT, scope JSONB, active_version_id UUID FK -> optimization_config_versions(id), updated_by TEXT, updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ). Uniqueness constraint: (config_key, scope_hash). `scope_hash` is a deterministic hash over the canonicalized scope JSON to avoid JSONB equality edge cases. Notes: - Scope is intentionally flexible JSON for now (tenant/model/region); canonicalization happens in the service layer. We can normalize later if needed. - Versions are immutable by design; future PRs will add promotion semantics, audit events, and safe-apply gating. - This PR does not attempt to migrate existing optimization configs; a follow-up PR will backfill current state into v1 records (tracked separately). Testing: - Added migration tests (apply + rollback) and repository unit tests for version creation, list ordering, and active pointer update behavior. - Added a simple API integration test that creates v1/v2 and reads them back. Rollout: - DB migration is additive. - API routes are behind `--enable-optimization-config-versioning` flag; no callers wired in yet. Follow-ups: ENG-4822 diff + semantic validators; ENG-4824 canary rollout controller; ENG-4826 audit log events; ENG-4823 runtime applier idempotency integration; migration/backfill PR for existing configs.
commits: control-plane: add scope canonicalization + scope_hash helper
control-plane: repository methods for create/list/get versions + set active pointer
api: internal endpoints for versions CRUD (flagged)
tests: migration and repository unit tests
review_conversation: Ethan Park: Data model looks aligned with the ADR direction (immutable versions + mutable pointer). Can we enforce immutability at the DB layer (no updates) or is it convention-only?

Michael Nguyen (author): Good call. I added a DB trigger to prevent UPDATE on optimization_config_versions, except for a narrow allowlist of no-op fields. In practice we shouldn't update anything; the trigger makes it explicit. Also made the service reject update attempts.
Benji Okafor: For optimization_config_active, JSONB scope uniqueness is tricky. How are we ensuring two semantically identical scopes don’t create duplicate active rows?

Michael Nguyen (author): Added `scope_hash` computed from canonical JSON (sorted keys, normalized arrays) and use (config_key, scope_hash) uniqueness. The canonicalization helper is used by both create+lookup paths so we don’t drift.
Jordan Lee: Please make sure `created_by` is not user-supplied from the request body; it should come from auth context. Also, do we need `source` for later auditability?

Michael Nguyen (author): Updated route handler to ignore any created_by passed by client and use ctx.actor instead. Added `source` field ("console" | "api" | "terraform" | "migration") with a default of "api" for now; full audit events will come in ENG-4826.
Chloe Martin: Small API nit: list endpoint should support pagination and stable ordering for the Console timeline later. Can we add `limit` + `cursor` now?
Michael Nguyen (author): Added `limit` (default 50, max 200) and cursor based on (created_at, id). Ordering is DESC created_at, then DESC id. Included in integration tests.
Benji Okafor: I’m worried about concurrent writes to set the active pointer during rollouts. Do we need locking?

Michael Nguyen (author): Active pointer updates are a single transaction with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the active row by (config_key, scope_hash). If missing, we insert and rely on uniqueness + retry on conflict. Added a unit test for the race path.
Ethan Park: Looks good after the immutability trigger + pagination. Approving.
notable_snippet: Migration adds immutable table + constraints: CREATE TABLE optimization_config_versions ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), config_key TEXT NOT NULL, version INT NOT NULL, scope JSONB NOT NULL, payload JSONB NOT NULL, payload_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, created_by TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), comment TEXT, source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'api', UNIQUE (config_key, version) ); CREATE INDEX idx_opt_cfg_versions_key_created_at ON optimization_config_versions (config_key, created_at DESC);
